summary.intent: Build a full interactive TUI dashboard for the memory-loop subsystem using Charmbracelet/bubbletea libraries, with 4 tabs (Memories, Injection, History, Settings) and full CRUD/lifecycle management.
summary.outcome: A working TUI was built and committed across multiple iterations. Core functionality works (memories tab, settings cycling, injection prompt tester) but visual polish is still in progress — settings tab styling doesn't match the mockup design.

repo: The CLI uses a `termstyle` package for ANSI 256-color theming that respects NO_COLOR; new TUI should use color codes from this palette rather than hardcoded hex.
The `docs/superpowers/` directory is gitignored — brainstorm artifacts and specs written there won't appear in git history.
Existing package structure follows `cmd/entire/cli/<feature>/` pattern; new TUI package placed at `cmd/entire/cli/memorylooptui/`.
ACCESSIBLE=1 env var is used throughout the CLI for screen-reader fallbacks; TUI falls back to plain-text show subcommand when set.
Memory loop state lives in `.entire/memory-loop.json`; must run `entire memory-loop refresh` before TUI has data to display.

code.finding: The tea.KeyMsg case in the root Update method processes global keys then exits the case block. Delegation to sub-tabs happens outside the switch at ~line 175 using the outer tea.Msg parameter — type assertion back to tea.KeyMsg works because the underlying value is preserved, but this is non-obvious.
Settings key handling was broken due to closure capture issues with pointer fields in settingsChangedMsg. Fixed by capturing the full struct value rather than pointer fields in the tea.Cmd closure.
Lipgloss color '8' (dark gray) is invisible on dark terminals — use '245' (light gray) for borders and inactive tab labels. Color '214' is the orange accent used throughout.
Log table height must be explicitly capped (e.g. h-10) to prevent content overflow that pushes the tab bar off-screen entirely.
Detail pane width must be set to `width - 2` unconditionally (not gated on width > 0) to ensure lipgloss border renders. Border color must be '245' not '8'.

workflow: Subagent-driven development worked well for parallelizing independent tab implementations but caused integration issues (uncommitted changes across agents, fix agents committing mid-session).
The brainstorm visual companion server shuts down between sessions and must be restarted; content must be re-written to the new session path.
Adding debug file logging (writing to /tmp) is a viable debugging technique for bubbletea apps where you can't use stdout — helped isolate the settings key handling bug.
Lipgloss v1 border API requires explicit width setting relative to terminal width; borders silently fail to render if width is 0 or unset.
When a subagent commits fixes, the parent session may not see those commits in `git diff` — always run `git log` to verify what was actually committed before committing again.

friction: Lipgloss border color '8' is invisible on dark terminals — wasted multiple iterations debugging 'missing borders' that were actually just invisible.
Settings tab key handling was silently broken for the entire session until debug logging was added; no error surfaced, keys were simply swallowed.
The brainstorm visual companion server doesn't persist between sessions, requiring manual restart and content re-creation.
Subagent-driven execution led to uncommitted changes across multiple agents, requiring manual cleanup and re-committing at the end.
Terminal width cap of 80 columns was too narrow for the user's terminal, causing layout issues that weren't caught in code review.
Injection tab overflow (pushing tab bar off-screen) required multiple fix attempts before the correct height cap was found.
open_items: Settings tab visual design still doesn't match the mockup — needs a single-panel row layout rather than individual bordered cards per setting.
History tab 'R' refresh trigger is a placeholder; async refresh with spinner not wired to actual memoryloop.Refresh() call.
Injection tab prompt tester may not be fully functional — user noted it 'doesn't seem like prompt injection works'.
No unit tests for any of the TUI components — manual verification only.
Injection log detail card when selecting a log entry may not be rendering correctly.
The 9-task plan included 'fmt, lint, test:ci, manual verification checklist' as Task 9 — tests were skipped as explicitly deferred.
Async spinner state for refresh operations was deferred from the History tab implementation.
The `prune` action (x keybinding) was added late in spec review — may not be fully implemented in the memories tab lifecycle actions.
